It evaluates LLMs of varying scale against specialized generative models on statistical fidelity, downstream utility, and privacy risk, finding LLMs generally superior but more privacy-vulnerable, with curation improving the privacy-utility tradeoff. CTGAN is named only in passing as one of several specialized GAN architectures for tabular generation cited in the related-work discussion.
evidence: "Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have introduced specialized architectures including CTGAN [3], PATEGAN [4], ADSGAN [5], and GANBLR [6] that address various aspects of tabular generation challenges."
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Mining Workshops (ICDMW)
needs: Full text not obtained; unclear whether CTGAN was actually run as one of the 'specialized generative models' compared in the empirical evaluation, or only cited in the related-work list.

title: Loan Default Prediction Using CTGAN-MLP
summary: This conference paper proposes a hybrid CTGAN-MLP model for loan default prediction, using CTGAN to generate balanced synthetic tabular data to counter class imbalance and an MLP classifier to improve prediction accuracy over traditional machine learning baselines. Experiments show the CTGAN-MLP combination improves identification of minority (default) samples in financial risk data. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run as the generator producing the synthetic minority-class training data underpinning the entire empirical evaluation.
evidence: "This study proposes a hybrid CTGAN-MLP model, which employs the Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) to generate balanced synthetic data..."

title: Local-Support Guided Latent Generation for Reliable Minority-Class Augmentation in Network Intrusion Detection
summary: A conference paper proposing a latent-generation method to synthesize reliable minority-class samples for network intrusion detection, aiming to improve detection of rare attack types under class imbalance. The related-work section situates the approach among mixed-type tabular generators, naming CTGAN, TabDDPM, and TabSyn as prior expressive generative methods. CTGAN is only cited as an example of a mixed-type data generator, with no evidence it was run or compared against.
evidence: "More expressive mixed-type generators include CTGAN [4], TabDDPM [5], and latent-space methods such as TabSyn [6]."

title: Location data privacy protection for the logistics order data publishing in intelligent logistics big data platform
summary: This paper addresses privacy protection for location-based logistics order data prior to its publication on an intelligent logistics big data platform, proposing a scheme aimed at preserving sensitive location information while retaining data utility for downstream analytics. Based on the available metadata, no full text or abstract was obtained, so the paper's technical approach cannot be described in detail. The work cites the original Synthetic Data Vault (SDV) paper, suggesting SDV is referenced as related work on synthetic data generation for privacy-preserving data publishing.

title: LogiCoTab: Controllable Tabular Data Synthesis with Logical Relationships Awareness
summary: This paper proposes LogiCoTab, a two-stage tabular data synthesis method that first extracts semantic features and inter-column logical relationships, then uses a diffusion-based generative model for controllable, logically consistent synthesis. It targets the problem that existing methods rely on lossy encoding of mixed-type tabular data, causing logical inconsistencies in synthetic output. CTGAN is cited in the related-work discussion of GAN-based tabular synthesis schemes and one-hot encoding approaches, without evidence it was run as an experimental baseline.
evidence: CTGAN is cited among references [4]-[6] in the sentence 'Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely explored for tabular data generation [4]-[6], [15], [22]', a generic related-work mention with no described experimental use.

title: Longitudinal Synthetic Data Generation by Artificial Intelligence to Accelerate Clinical and Translational Research in Breast Cancer
summary: This study applies GANs, VAEs, and language models to generate synthetic longitudinal clinical data for HER2-positive and triple-negative breast cancer patients drawn from the i2b2 platform, aiming to overcome privacy and fragmentation limits of real-world data. The authors evaluate fidelity, utility, and privacy of the synthetic data using their own framework, SAFE, and test it in privacy-preserving data integration, multistate disease modeling, and synthetic control-arm generation for trials. The SDV paper is cited alongside other synthetic-data evaluation frameworks that SAFE 'integrates and extends,' with no indication that SDV's software was itself run.
evidence: "SAFE integrates and extends methods from existing frameworks for SD evaluation, 36-38 aiming to address key limitations in their application to longitudinal and domain-specific clinical contexts."
needs: Only abstract and citing sentence available; full text not seen, so it is unclear whether SDV software/metrics were actually run or merely cited as prior evaluation framework literature.

title: Low-sample classification in NIDS using the EC-GAN method
summary: This paper adapts the semi-supervised EC-GAN framework to tabular network-flow data, replacing its original image-domain GAN with a Wasserstein Conditional GAN with Gradient Penalty (WCGAN-GP) to generate synthetic samples that help a DNN classifier trained on small, imbalanced slices of the CIC-IDS-2017 intrusion-detection dataset. The authors show their modified EC-GAN can match prior detection results using as little as 25% of the original data. CTGAN and TGAN (Xu et al. 2019; Xu & Veeramachaneni 2018) are named as alternative tabular-data GAN solutions the authors considered before choosing WCGAN-GP, but neither is implemented or run.
evidence: "As possible alternative to WCGAN-GP we considered TGAN [Xu and Veeramachaneni,2018] and [Xu et al.,2019], which are two well-known solutions for tabular data generation."
needs: CTGAN/TGAN are only briefly discussed as considered alternatives, not run; confirms citation_only rather than baseline_only.

summary: This paper proposes an electricity theft detection system for smart meters that combines LSTM-based feature extraction with a bat-algorithm-tuned RUSBoost classifier to address class imbalance, overfitting, and high-dimensional time-series data, showing improved F1-score and ROC performance over SVM, CNN, and logistic regression baselines. The CTGAN paper is cited only as the source of a normalization equation and appears unconnected to any actual use of the CTGAN model or its methodology.

title: Machine-Learning-Based Adaptive Wireless Network Selection for Terrestrial and Non-Terrestrial Networks in 5G and Beyond
summary: This paper proposes a machine-learning approach to decide between terrestrial and non-terrestrial network connectivity in a human-centric, multi-connectivity 5G/6G smart-city scenario, using a synthetic sensor-based dataset to train classifiers such as Gradient Boosting, Neural Networks, Random Forest, and kNN. To build the 30,000-sample dataset used for all downstream ML experiments, the authors train a CTGAN model (300 epochs, batch size 500, learning rate 2e-4, latent dimension 128) to synthesize tabular data. CTGAN, the conditional tabular GAN from the SDV family, is run directly as the sole synthetic data generator underpinning the entire empirical evaluation.
evidence: "an ultimate dataset that contains 30,000 samples is obtained via a generative adversarial networks (GAN)-based deep learning data synthesizer named the conditional tabular generative adversarial network (CTGAN)... The CTGAN model is trained for 300 epochs with a batch size of 500, learning rate 2x10-4, and latent dimension of 128."

title: Using machine learning to assist auditory processing evaluation
summary: This clinical study applies Random Forest and XGBoost, interpreted with SHAP, to categorize children referred for auditory processing disorder (APD) assessment into clinical sub-groups matching expert audiologist labels, using retrospective data from 134 children. Because the dataset was small and imbalanced, the authors used CTGAN as a data augmentation technique to generate synthetic training samples, comparing it against SMOTE and reporting it significantly improved neural network accuracy. CTGAN, SDV's conditional tabular GAN with mode-specific normalization and training-by-sampling for imbalanced columns, is run as one of the augmentation methods evaluated in the study.
affiliations: Western University; University of Southern Mississippi
evidence: "Here, we used the CTGAN augmentation technique (Xu et al., 2019)... CTGAN did significantly improve the results when used with a Neural Network."

title: Machine Learning Assisted Stroke Prediction in Mechanical Circulatory Support: Predictive Role of Systemic Mitochondrial Dysfunction
summary: This study examines systemic mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation abnormalities as predictors of postoperative stroke in continuous-flow left ventricular assist device patients, using LASSO and Random Forest models on blood leukocyte protein data to achieve an AUC of 0.93. The authors describe balancing their small clinical dataset with SMOTE oversampling rather than any SDV-family tool. The citation to the CTGAN paper appears in the sentence describing this SMOTE-based class balancing, with no evidence CTGAN itself was run.

needs: Full text not available; the citation appears attached to a SMOTE description rather than any CTGAN usage, so it is unclear whether CTGAN was used elsewhere in the paper or this is purely a mis-citation.

title: Machine Learning-Driven Prediction of Gleason Score 7 Prostate Cancer Patterns Using Multi-Omics Data
summary: This study builds a prostate cancer prediction system that combines DNA methylation, gene expression, copy number alteration, and gene-mutation features to distinguish the clinically similar Gleason Score 3+4 and 4+3 grade-7 cancer subtypes, using PCA, autoencoders, and tuned ML/ANN classifiers for binary classification. To address severe class imbalance between the two Gleason subtypes, the authors describe using 'a custom Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN)' to synthesize minority-class samples, citing the CTGAN NeurIPS 2019 paper. CTGAN's conditional generative approach is the mechanism used to balance the training dataset before downstream classification.
evidence: "a custom Conditional Tabular Generative Adversarial Network (CTGAN) [14] was used to generate synthetic samples for the minority classes 4 + 3, giving rise to 290 samples."

title: Machine Learning for Failure Management in Microwave Networks: A Data-Centric Approach
summary: This paper proposes a Data-Centric approach for hardware-failure classification in microwave networks, using Conditional Variational Autoencoders to synthetically augment imbalanced training data and Batch Uncertainty-based Active Learning to guide data annotation. On a real-world dataset from a microwave equipment vendor, the CVAE-based augmentation is shown to outperform two state-of-the-art baselines. CTGAN is run as one of these baselines, generating synthetic minority-class samples that are compared against the authors' CVAE and against SMOTE in quantitative accuracy/F1 tables.
evidence: "We consider two state-of-the-art baselines, namely, CTGAN and SMOTE, that add synthetic data to the training set and balance the per-class representation." CTGAN results are reported in Tables II and III alongside CVAE and SMOTE.
venue: IEEE Transactions on Network and Service Management
